core_obligations: Pass to the blowing up (proof lines 4829-4837): by the injectivity axiom it suffices to prove the vanishing after pulling back along the blowing up of the subscheme.

Rewrite the pulled back class (proof lines 4837-4845): the compatibility of the cycle class map with pullback identifies the pulled back class of the subscheme with the product of the class of the exceptional divisor with the class of the auxiliary cycle, and the class of the exceptional divisor is the first Chern class of the corresponding invertible module.

Conclude (proof lines 4845-4850): the pulled back class restricts to zero on the exceptional divisor, so the axiom on cup products with divisor classes gives the vanishing, which is what had to be shown.
proof_roadmap: Reduce by the injectivity axiom to the blowing up.
Rewrite the pulled back class as a product with the class of the exceptional divisor.
Apply the divisor axiom to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if a cohomology class restricts to zero on a smooth closed subscheme whose conormal class in K theory is a restriction of a class on the ambient scheme, then its cup product with the cycle class of the subscheme vanishes (statement lines 4825-4835). The proof (proof lines 4836-4850) passes to the blowing up, rewrites the pulled back class through the exceptional divisor, and applies the divisor axiom. H2: a complete short argument in three steps.
